sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Context**: The Kheda district faced severe drought and plague, leading to a crop yield of less than 25% of the normal produce.
• **Legal Provision**: Under the **Revenue Code**, if the yield was less than 1/4th of the normal, farmers were entitled to a total remission of land revenue.
• **Government Stance**: The colonial administration refused to acknowledge the crop failure and insisted on full collection, threatening to confiscate land and property.
• **Leadership**: Mahatma Gandhi provided the moral framework, while **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel**, Indulal Yagnik, and Shankarlal Banker provided the organizational ground-level leadership.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Non-violent, mass-based agrarian protest in Kheda, Gujarat.
Violation of Revenue Code regarding crop failure remissions.
Transition of Gandhi from urban/industrial to rural peasant politics.
Government agreed to suspend collection for the current year and the next.
Restoration of confiscated property; revenue collection made flexible.
Established the 'Patidar' peasantry as a potent political force.

items.definition: The legal framework governing land tax; the movement challenged the government's arbitrary interpretation of 'normal yield'.
A formal vow taken by peasants to refuse tax payment, emphasizing the moral superiority of the cause over colonial law.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Mass Mobilization**: Use of 'Sabhas' and door-to-door campaigning to build solidarity among diverse peasant castes.
• **Institutional Building**: The movement served as a training ground for the Gujarat Sabha, which later became the Gujarat Provincial Congress Committee.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Challenges**: Fear of land confiscation and government repression; internal divisions within the peasantry.
• **Solutions**: Gandhi's insistence on 'Satyagraha' (truth-force) ensured that even the poorest peasants remained committed to the cause.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'K-A-C' (Kheda, Ahmedabad, Champaran).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Chronological order of Gandhi's early experiments: Champaran (1917), Ahmedabad (1918), Kheda (1918).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses Kheda with Bardoli. Remember: Kheda (1918) was about crop failure/remission; Bardoli (1928) was about tax hike protest.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Peasant-Nationalist Synergy' to describe how local agrarian grievances were integrated into the broader national freedom struggle.

keyTakeaways: Kheda was the first instance of a 'No-Tax' campaign in the Gandhian era.
It solidified the alliance between the urban intelligentsia and the rural peasantry.
The movement proved that the British government could be forced to negotiate if the resistance was organized and non-violent.
